Home / Hydro jetting and drain lines in Ogden

Drain and sewer cleaning for Ogden homes

Ogden is one of the oldest towns in Riley County. It sits on the Kansas River and the Union Pacific line, about 11 miles southwest of Manhattan and next to Fort Riley. Homes here range from railroad-era houses to newer builds, and the type of sewer service varies by property, so a drain problem starts with a simple question: city sewer or a private system?

{{PHONE_DISPLAY}}Describe your drain problem

City sewer, septic or something else

Hydro jetting applies to sewer and drain lines only. If your home is on a septic system, a different service is needed. Records or a qualified professional can confirm what you have.

Old town, old laterals

A house from Ogden's early decades may still have its original lateral with undocumented repairs. A camera inspection is the way to learn its material and condition.

Trees in the river valley

Ogden lies along the Kansas River, and valley trees put out roots that find moisture easily. Roots can enter older joints and reduce flow, which is why recurring clogs here are worth a root check.

Related reading

These pages explain what to look for in an older small-town line.

How Hydro Jetting WorksTree Root IntrusionsHydro Jetting vs Snaking

Questions about this drain problem

Is Ogden on city sewer?

It depends on the property. Records or a qualified professional can confirm for your address.

Why check for roots in a river valley?

Moist ground draws roots toward buried joints. A camera shows whether growth has entered the line.

How old can an Ogden lateral be?

Some may date from the town's early years, though many have been repaired. Only an inspection can say.

Tell us what is happening with your drains.

Whether the issue is a kitchen line that keeps clogging or a main sewer backup, describe the symptoms and how long they have been going on. A drain professional can determine whether hydro jetting is suitable after reviewing the line.
